title: The Ransom of Red Chief
text:
Sam and Bill, two small time crooks, needed money for a land swindle. In a sleepy Alabama town they kidnapped the ten year old son of Ebenezer Dorset, a prosperous citizen, and hid him in a cave in the hills. They planned to ask two thousand dollars for his return.

The boy was delighted. He announced that he was Red Chief, terror of the plains, and that Bill was his captive. He kept them awake all night with war whoops, tried to scalp Bill at daybreak, dropped a hot potato down his back, hit him with a stone from a sling, and rode him like a horse for what Bill claimed was ninety miles. He had no intention of going home.

By the second day Bill was a wreck. Sam lowered the ransom demand to fifteen hundred dollars and sent the letter. Dorset's reply was polite. He thought their demands a little high, and made a counter offer: if they brought Johnny home and paid him two hundred and fifty dollars in cash, he would agree to take the boy off their hands. They had better come at night, he added, because the neighbors believed the boy was lost and he could not answer for what they might do.

The kidnappers paid. At midnight they handed over the screaming boy, and while his father held him, they ran for the Canadian border.
lesson: A plan built on what you assume the other side values can collapse when you learn what they actually value. Know your counterpart before you set terms.
people: Sam, Bill Driscoll, Johnny Dorset, Ebenezer Dorset
source: O. Henry, The Ransom of Red Chief (1907; collected in Whirligigs, 1910)
